owner: CC (code + proofs); Akien (the intention, the format, and the retention model — 'i can think of 10M times that woulda been handy')
intention: A FLIGHT RECORDER FOR BASH: source it, and what a script tried, what came back, and what it returned becomes a durable record instead of scrollback. One append-only file per namespace, capped at the last N lines, every line stamped <yyyymmdd.hhmmss.uuuuuu>.<pid> so concurrent shells stay separable. A child process renames the namespace for its own lifetime and leaves the parent's untouched — which is just how export works, so it costs nothing. Its first tenant is the boot: superclaude and launchers/bootstrap.sh route their steps through it, which is what makes the launcher's WATCHME emittable at all.
why: Akien, 2026-07-30, on the superclaude preflight: 'this is booting, it's a little weird, but it should log what the script tried, what worked, what didn't... i can think of 10M times that woulda been handy, just to have that running in the background.' Booting is precisely the moment when nothing else is up yet to observe you, so the launcher has to observe itself. And Law 3: a boot that leaves no record leaves every later question about it — did the repair run? did it work? was it slow? — to be re-derived by guessing, which is the defect Law 1 names.
traces_to: Law 3 (nothing is known until measured) — a boot that leaves no record cannot be reasoned about, only guessed at

Law 7 (loud at diagnostic surfaces, permanent in records of truth) — this is a DIAGNOSTIC surface, and the charter says so where it matters: the trim's small race is acceptable HERE and would not be in a record of truth
Law 1 (the resolver is spent on the novel) — the answer to 'what happened last boot' becomes a file instead of a re-derivation
the rescue ethos (launchers/intention+why.json) — it must never be able to break the shell that sourced it

watchme.trigger: Every ground_loop pulse reaching bin's watcher. The probe reads the LOG DIRECTORY only (~/.cairn/logs, or $CAIRN_LOGDIR) — a listing plus a line-scan per namespace, no device, no bus, no network, so it is cheap enough to sit on a pulse. For each file whose lines parse as this recorder's grammar (<yyyymmdd.hhmmss.uuuuuu>.<pid>: <msg>) it counts retained lines, DISTINCT PIDS, and surviving `logtrim:` marks. A namespace has TURNED OVER when its window is full (retained >= CAIRN_LOGLEN) or a mark says it cut. It is a PEEPHOLE when it has turned over and now holds fewer than 2 distinct pids — a record that cannot show a previous run cannot answer 'what changed', which is the flight recorder's entire job. FIRES when >= 2 namespaces have turned over AND at least one is a peephole.
watchme.enough: CLEARED once >= 2 namespaces have turned over AND none is a peephole: 1000 survived contact with both shipped traffic profiles — `bash` (interactive, one record per output line, bursty) and `boot` (a launcher, ~8 records per launch, metronomic) — which differ by orders of magnitude on the only axis a retention question varies along. THE SAME TURNOVER FLOOR IS ON BOTH PREDICATES, deliberately: without it the watch would clear on a fresh install where no namespace has ever filled and therefore none can be a peephole — a watch that retires before it could ever fire, which is the defect watchme-emits-a-probe shipped with and paid for on 2026-07-30. If 1000 later stops holding, that is a NEW watch carried deliberately, not this one silently resuming.
watchme.carrier: A dict carried by the probe's `carry`: which namespaces went blind, the window they went blind at, and the full per-namespace rows (retained / runs / trim_marks) so the owner sizes the new number off the evidence instead of guessing a second time. A POINTER to this ticket rides along, never a copy of it (Law 6 — the ticket is the commons').
watchme.nexus: hypothesize — the tree that remembers what killed which. '1000 is enough' is a prediction made before any traffic existed to size it against; a prediction that did not hold belongs where predictions are buried.
watchme.consumer: AKIEN, through the owner's gate. The probe deposits and pokes; moving CAIRN_LOGLEN is the owner's act, not the probe's (Law 6). What it can do is put a measured 'namespace X has turned over and now speaks for one live process' in front of him.

distinctions_recorded: HALF A FIX READS EXACTLY LIKE A WHOLE ONE. Defect (3) was 'quoting is lost'. I fixed the EXECUTION ("$@") and then rendered the RECORD with $*, which re-joined on spaces and threw the argument boundaries away again. The bug lived in the artifact, and the artifact is the thing nobody re-checks. Caught only because the smoke test looked at the log file rather than at the return code.

A GENERAL INVARIANT BELONGS AT THE DOOR, NOT IN THE CALLERS. Wiring the boot revealed that a multi-line message produced multiple records, all but the first unstamped. The fix could have been 'callers pass single-line text' — but the interesting messages are exactly the ones carrying captured output. Collapsing newlines in _logbash_write makes it hold for every caller instead of for the ones who remembered.

LOGRUN RUNS ITS ARGUMENT IN A PIPELINE, HENCE A SUBSHELL. Wrapping cairn_bootstrap_verify in logrun would have silently discarded CAIRN_BOOTSTRAP_FINDINGS and left the report empty — a logging tool erasing the thing being logged. Only real subprocesses get logrun; state-mutating shell functions get lognote at their decision points.

THE COMMAND-SUBSTITUTION NEWLINE TRAP, AS A VACUITY BUG. $(printf '\n') is the empty string — command substitution strips trailing newlines. A fixture built that way is silently single-line, which is trap (b) from the standing lesson: a fixture that never reaches the branch under test cannot fail.

A KEPT COPY IS NOT MORE EVIDENCE (2026-07-30, the retention probe's first live fire). The survey walked ~/.cairn/logs and reported TWO namespaces — `boot` with 19 runs and `boot.pre-decontamination` with 54 — the second being a pre-image parked beside the record an hour earlier while cleaning a contamination out of it. Nothing about a backup distinguishes it from a namespace: same grammar, same recorder, same directory. The fix is physics rather than a name to remember — anything KEPT rather than WRITTEN lives in a subdirectory now, and a subdirectory is not a file, so it cannot be surveyed at all. Twice in one afternoon the same shape: a copy of the evidence counted as more evidence.
filed_edges: INTERACTIVE OUTPUT IS NOT CAPTURED. logbash_attach records every typed line and its real exit code via PROMPT_COMMAND, but bash exposes no hook in a command's data path — DEBUG fires before, PROMPT_COMMAND after. The only routes are a pty recorder (script(1): escape codes, no command boundaries) or redirecting the shell's own stdout through a tee (which full-screen programs fight). Both are real and neither is free; this is a separate stone with its own trade, not a flag to bolt on.

THE TRIM RACE IS ACKNOWLEDGED, NOT CLOSED. flock serialises trims against each other, but `tee -a` holds no lock, so a line can be lost between the tail and the rewrite. Acceptable because this is a diagnostic surface (Law 7); a record of truth would need its own door, not a retrofit onto logtrim.

TWO COMPONENTS AT ONE ADDRESS. bin/ now holds the dispatcher (cairn-command) and this, under one intention+why.json — the same second-facility pattern as launchers/bootstrap.sh and the tester's verb. Fine while both are PATH-resident tooling of the same node_class; if the logger grows its own voyage it wants its own address (Law 5).

THE INSTALL IS NOT APPLIED ON THIS BOX. cairn_logger_install is written, idempotent, backs up, and is proven — but ~/.bashrc has not been edited. Until it is, interactive shells are not recorded and the host-seam's seal is unclaimed rather than stale.
watchme_prose: PROSE PRECURSOR to the spec above, kept as the reasoning it was compiled from. logtrim writes `logtrim: discarded N lines, window now starts at <stamp>` into the record itself before every cut (bin/logger_for_bash), pinned by test_a_trim_leaves_evidence_that_it_trimmed. QUESTION IT ANSWERS, which needs TIME and cannot be settled by any proof: is 1000 lines the right window? A retention window is only ever discovered to be wrong IN HINDSIGHT — someone reaches back for a boot the file no longer holds, at exactly the moment they cannot afford to discover it — so the discard has to leave a mark or the miss is invisible. THE MEASURE SHARPENED when the probe was built: not 'how many hours does the window span' (which needs a clock) but 'can it still show TWO RUNS' — a record that has turned over and now speaks for a single live process has stopped being a record and become a peephole onto the present, which is the one thing the process could already see.
